body.statement: Conditional on the effective-compatible-density theorem, every finite atomic Gaussian dual certificate is contained in a compact local direction set admitting a lawful multinomial realization whose dual value differs by the explicit positive-cell comparison remainder. With \(M_n=\inf_{K_n\in\mathcal C_{n,\eta_0}}\sup_{u\in H_{n,r_0}}E_{p_n(u)}[\ell_0\{K_n(N_n)\}]\), taking certificate accuracy to zero before exhausting compact sets yields \(\liminf_{n\to\infty}M_n\ge M_{\mathfrak G_0,\eta_0}(r_0)\), while the transferred primal rules yield the reverse \(\limsup\) inequality under the moving-offset schedule.
body.justification: The order of limits prevents an unjustified bounded-support assumption on least-favorable dual mass.
body.gap: Neither Carter's global deficiency statement nor compact-parameter minimax approximation identifies the two-stage certificate-then-exhaustion argument for an unbounded local fan.
body.consumer: The Job Corps replay archive can interpret the certified \(\mathfrak G_0\) risk interval as the local multinomial minimax benchmark for the same declared assertion list, rather than as an unverified Gaussian upper approximation.

obligation.what_is_open: Prove the proposed zero-offset, certificate-first lower transfer with a theorem-level quantitative multinomial comparison.
obligation.obstruction: The original two-sided statement is too strong under mere \(p_n(0)\to p_0\), and the remaining honest lower statement still needs the undeclared quantitative Carter comparison used by the fixed-stratum target.
obligation.attempted: The drift counterexample isolates the missing zero-offset condition. After narrowing, the finite-support order of limits is valid, but its numerical comparison remainder cannot be certified from the current core.
obligation.partial_result: After imposing \(c_n\to0\), every fixed finite collection of active slacks and every fixed compact collection of parameter points has the zero-offset geometry eventually away from a vanishing boundary band. Thus a finite Gaussian dual is the correct lower-bound object; the unresolved step is the quantitative two-way multinomial comparison at its atoms.
